chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 53 — The Unfilled Valley and the Rest of the Righteous
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language witness available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text preserved in Rylands Ethiopic MS 23 is the translation base for all seven verses, including the deep unfilled valley receiving tribute, the self-consuming labor of sinners, angels preparing instruments of the Satan, the destruction of earthly rulers, and the appearance of the Chosen One's assembly. The singular title the Satan and the witness's imagery of flattened mountains and water-like hills are retained. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: There my eyes saw a deep valley with its mouth open. All who dwell upon the dry ground, the sea, and the islands will bring it gifts, offerings, and tribute, yet that deep valley will not be filled.
verses.study: The open valley consumes the world's wealth without satisfaction. Tribute that once maintained earthly power now flows into an emptiness that cannot be filled.
crossReferences: Proverbs 27:20 — Sheol and destruction are never satisfied
Habakkuk 2:5 — arrogant appetite gathers nations yet is never filled
Revelation 18:11–17 — global wealth collapses with an oppressive city

verses.text: Their hands commit wrongdoing, and sinners consume everything for which people labor wrongfully. The sinners will perish from before the face of the Lord of Spirits, be driven from the face of His earth, and cease forever and ever.
verses.study: Wrongful labor feeds a system consumed by sinners rather than sustaining life. Judgment removes both the perpetrators and the exploitative pattern from the Lord's earth.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 2:26 — the sinner gathers only to hand the gain away
Micah 2:1–3 — hands that devise wrongdoing meet an inescapable judgment
Psalm 104:35 — sinners finally vanish from the earth

verses.text: For I saw the angels of punishment going and preparing all the instruments of the Satan.
verses.study: Punishment is neither accidental nor uncontrolled. Heavenly agents prepare instruments associated with the accuser for judgment, placing even terror under appointed administration.
crossReferences: 2 Samuel 24:16 — an angelic agent of judgment acts under divine restraint
Matthew 25:41 — judgment includes fire prepared for the devil and his angels
Revelation 20:1–3 — a heavenly agent carries instruments to restrain the deceiver

verses.text: I asked the angel of peace who went with me, 'For whom are they preparing these instruments?'
verses.study: Enoch seeks the intended objects of judgment rather than speculating from the frightening equipment. The angel of peace interprets instruments of punishment within a larger purpose of restored peace.
crossReferences: Zechariah 1:9 — an accompanying angel answers the prophet's question
Daniel 7:16 — the seer asks for the truth of what he sees
Revelation 7:13–14 — a heavenly guide identifies those in the vision

verses.text: He said to me, 'They are preparing them for the kings and the mighty of this earth, so that they may be destroyed by them.'
verses.study: The instruments target rulers whose power seemed protected by tribute and wealth. The vision makes political might accountable rather than exempt.
crossReferences: Psalm 76:12 — God cuts off the spirit of rulers
Isaiah 24:21 — the kings of the earth are punished
Revelation 19:18–21 — kings and mighty people meet judgment with the beastly order

verses.text: After this the Righteous and Chosen One will cause the house of his assembly to appear, and from then on they will not be hindered in the name of the Lord of Spirits.
verses.study: The purpose beyond judgment is a visible, unhindered assembly. The Chosen One creates space for a community that lives openly and securely in the Lord's name.
crossReferences: Isaiah 4:5–6 — God creates shelter over the gathered holy community
Matthew 16:18 — the chosen ruler builds an assembly that hostile powers cannot overcome
Revelation 21:2–3 — the holy dwelling appears as God's home with His people

verses.text: Before his face these mountains will be like level ground, and the hills will be like a fountain of water, and the righteous will have rest from the oppression of sinners.
verses.study: Obstacles become level and sources of refreshment as oppression ends. Rest for the righteous is the constructive result of the Chosen One's victory over entrenched power.
crossReferences: Isaiah 40:4 — mountains and hills are leveled before God's coming
Isaiah 41:18 — God turns hills into springs of water
2 Thessalonians 1:6–7 — the afflicted receive rest when oppressors are judged

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 53 develops the collapse of metal power into a judgment on the economic and political systems built around it. Gifts and tribute pour into a deep valley that can never be filled.
Human labor is corrupted when wrongdoing consumes its fruit. The Lord's judgment therefore addresses not only individual rulers but a pattern in which powerful sinners feed upon the work of others.

The angels' prepared instruments are directed toward kings and mighty people, ending the immunity claimed by status and wealth. The angel of peace explains the punishment because its final aim is relief from oppression.
The Righteous and Chosen One then reveals an unhindered assembly. Level ground, flowing water and rest replace mountains of domination, unfilled appetite and the exhausting labor imposed by sinners.

crossReferences: Proverbs 27:20; Habakkuk 2:5 — appetite and destruction never satisfied
Isaiah 24:21 — judgment of earthly kings
Isaiah 40:4; 41:18 — leveled mountains and water from hills
2 Thessalonians 1:6–7 — rest for the oppressed
Revelation 21:2–3 — the appearing holy assembly and dwelling
